    "Agent thanked the customer warmly and personally: \"شكرًا على كلامك الجميل يا فندم...\"",
    "Agent avoided asking for the perfume name or asking the customer to retype/clarify — correctly treated the messages as compliments rather than a product lookup.",
    "Second reply varied wording (\"بنشكر اختيارك لعطور Perfamix\") so it did not repeat the first reply word-for-word.",
    "No unsolicited recommendations, pricing, or offers were pushed into a compliment thread — respects the store rule not to pitch here."
  ],
  "failures": [
    {
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "human_feel",
      "what": "Both replies use very similar phrasing and the formal address 'يا فندم' twice.",
      "why_wrong": "While not prohibited, slightly repetitive/formal tone can feel templated rather than personally warm. The scenario required a warm, personal thank-you; a tiny bit more variation or a short personal touch would improve rapport.",
      "expected": "A top salesperson would add one different personal touch in the second reply (e.g., 'سعدنا إن العطر عجبك، ده يفرّحنا') or invite a light, non-pushy follow-up like leaving a review link."
    }
  ],
  "salesperson_verdict": "Acceptable: a sales manager would accept this turn — the agent followed the critical rules (thanked the customer, did not ask for the perfume name, did not pitch). A bit more natural variation would make it excellent."
